questions.def: We use 'have/has + past participle' for the present perfect tense.
questions.question: I ___ my homework already.

questions.def: 'She' takes 'has' in the present perfect.
questions.question: She ___ never been to Italy.

questions.def: The present perfect ('have/has lived') is needed, not 'are lived'.
questions.question: They are lived here for five years.

questions.def: Use present perfect 'has worked' for actions started in the past.
questions.question: He ___ at that company since 2015.

questions.def: Use 'Have' with 'you' in present perfect questions.
questions.question: ___ you ever eaten sushi?

questions.def: 'We' takes 'haven't' in the present perfect negative.
questions.question: We ___ finished our exams yet.

questions.def: Use 'have known' instead of 'am knowing' for states.
questions.question: I am knowing him for a long time.

questions.def: Use present perfect 'has seen' for repeated actions.
questions.question: She ___ that movie three times.

questions.def: Use 'had' in past perfect to describe an action before another.
questions.question: They ___ already left when I arrived.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had' shows an action before another in the past.
questions.question: Before I met her, I ___ never been in love.

questions.def: Use past perfect 'had eaten' for an action before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ all the cake before we arrived.

questions.def: Past perfect: 'had + past participle' for earlier past action.
questions.question: By the time I got there, she ___ already left.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: 'have/has been + -ing'.
questions.question: I ___ waiting for you for two hours!

questions.def: 'Has been learning' is correct, not 'is been learning'.
questions.question: She is been learning English for six months.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration: 'has been -ing'.
questions.question: It ___ all day.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: 'had been + -ing' before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ living here for ten years before they moved.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: 'had been + -ing' before a past event.
questions.question: He ___ studying all night when I saw him.

questions.def: 'Had been working' is correct, not 'was been working'.
questions.question: I was been working on this project all week.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: duration before a past event.
questions.question: She ___ for the bus for an hour when it finally arrived.

questions.def: Present perfect for experiences: 'has/have been to'.
questions.question: She ___ to Paris twice this year.

questions.def: 'You' takes 'have' in present perfect questions.
questions.question: How long ___ you known him?

questions.def: Present perfect for durations starting in the past.
questions.question: How long ___ you here?

questions.def: Use 'have' with 'I' in present perfect.
questions.question: I ___ never met anyone famous.

questions.def: Past perfect for an action completed before another.
questions.question: She ___ already eaten dinner when we arrived.

questions.def: 'Have been' is correct, not 'are been'.
questions.question: They are been friends since they were kids.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for recent actions.
questions.question: He ___ very hard lately.

questions.def: Present perfect: 'have/has been' for past experiences.
questions.question: I ___ to that restaurant before.

questions.def: Use 'Have' with 'you' to make a question.
questions.question: ___ you ever seen a ghost?

questions.def: We use 'have' with 'I' in the present perfect tense.
questions.question: I ___ never eaten sushi before today.

questions.def: Present perfect 'has lost' shows a past action with present result.
questions.question: She ___ her keys. She can't open the door.
